Rashi on Chullin 8a:10:1.hebrew: של עבודת כוכבים - שמשמשים בה קרבנות של עבודת כוכבים ואסורה בהנאה, כדאמרינן במסכת ע"ז (דף נא:): אבד תאבדון את כל המקומות - בכלים שנשתמשו לעבודת כוכבים הכתוב מדבר:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:10:1.english: [Used] for idol worship - Meaning that idolatrous offerings were served with it, and it is forbidden for benefit, as we say in tractate Avodah Zarah (page 51b): "You shall utterly destroy all the places" - Scripture speaks of vessels that were used for idol worship.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:10:2.hebrew: מקלקל הוא - ואין זו הנאה, שבחייה היו דמיה מרובין מלאחר שחיטה, שבחייה היא עומדת לג' דברים: לגדל ולדות, ולחרישה, ולאכילה:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:10:2.english: It is a matter of damage - This is not a benefit, since while it is alive its value was greater than after slaughter, for while it is alive it serves three purposes: to raise offspring, to plow, and to be eaten.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:10:3.english: To cut - This is a constructive act, since once he has slaughtered it, it now stands [to be used] for this [purpose].

Rashi on Chullin 8a:11:1.english: With a dangerously ill animal - Because it is [considered] an improvement and a benefit, since if he does not slaughter it, it will die.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:11:2.hebrew: באטמי דקיימי לקורבנא - נתחים טובים, ירך וכתף וחזה, דקיימי לשלחן דורון לאדם חשוב, וזה שחתכן הפסידן:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:11:2.english: With the choice cuts designated as a gift - Good cuts - the thigh, shoulder, and breast - which are set aside for the table, as a gift for an important person; and this one who cut them ruined them.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:12:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה - אף על גב דהוא מקלקל, אסור לחתוך משום שמנונית דאיסורא דנבלות שנבלעו בסכין:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:12:1.english: But let it be derived - Even though this [act of cutting] is a destructive act (not a normal act of deriving benefit), it is [nonetheless] forbidden to cut with it, because of the greasy residue of forbidden substance from the nevelot that has been absorbed into the knife.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:1.hebrew: ליבן - באור. בלשון חכמים נקרא ליבון, ובלשון הלועזים קורין באדמותי':
Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:1.english: Heated it - [Meaning,] with fire. In the language of the Sages it is called "libbun," and in the vernacular [Old French] it is called "ademoti" [related to the word for "red," i.e., heating something until it glows red-hot].

Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:2.hebrew: שחיטתו כשרה - ולא אמר שריפה היא זו ולא שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:2.english: His slaughter is valid - and it is not said that this is burning, not slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:3.english: Its sharpening takes precedence over its heating - He gets a head start and hurries to cut before the animal is burned by the fire.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:4.hebrew: והאיכא צדדין - דסכין כשנכנס לתוך החתך, קודם שתשחט רוב הסימנים, היא שורפת את הסימנים, ונמצאת שהיא נשרפה קודם שחיטה, שהרי ושט נקובתו במשהו ליטרף, ושריפה כנקב הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:4.english: But aren't there the sides [to worry about] - For the knife, when it enters into the cut, before it has slaughtered through the majority of the simanim, burns the simanim, and it turns out that it was burned before the slaughtering [was completed]; for a perforation of the esophagus by even the minutest amount renders [the animal] tereifah, and a burn is considered like a perforation.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:5.hebrew: מירווח רווח - מתרחב החתך מצדי הסכין מכאן ומכאן, ואין נוגע הסימן אלא חידודו של סכין:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:1:5.english: It spreads and widens - The cut widens from the sides of the knife, from here and from there, so that the trachea or esophagus is touched only by the sharpened edge of the knife.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:2:1.english: And struck with it - He strikes the person with force.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:2:2.hebrew: משום שחין נדון - לענין נגעים כדמפרש לקמן. שחין בא ע"י חום שמתחמם מחמת כח ההכאה, ומכוה באה מחמת האור, והכא דאיכא תרוייהו בהי מינייהו דיינינן ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:2:2.english: Is it judged as a boil - With regard to the halakhot of leprous marks, as [the Gemara] explains below. A boil comes about through heat generated by the force of the blow, whereas a burn comes about from fire; and here, since both factors are present, by which of the two do we judge it?

Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:1.english: For what practical difference - In what respect does the law of a burn (mechavah) differ from that of an inflammation (shechin), that you should raise this question?

Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:2.hebrew: מטמאים בשבוע אחד בשני סימנים בשער לבן ובפסיון - שאין בהן הסגר שני, כמו שכתוב (ויקרא יג) בשאת ובספחת ב' הסגרות, שאם עמד בעיניו ולא פשה שבוע ראשון מסגיר אותו בשניה שמא יפשה ויחליטנו, אבל בשחין ומכוה לא נאמר אלא הסגר אחד, ואם עמד בעיניו בשבוע ראשון שוב אין מסגירו לטמאו אלא פוטרו והולך:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:2.english: They become impure in one week by two signs: white hair and the spreading [of the lesion] - Because these have no second quarantine, as it is written (Leviticus 13) regarding a se'et and a sapachat [that there are] two quarantines: that if it remained as it was and did not spread during the first week, he quarantines it a second time, lest it spread and he then declare it a confirmed [tzara'at]. But regarding a boil and a burn, only one quarantine is stated; and if it remained as it was during the first week, he no longer quarantines it in order to declare it impure, but rather releases it [as pure], and moves on.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:3.english: With two signs - These, which it will specify [below].

Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:4.hebrew: שער לבן ופסיון - אם פשה, ולא כנתק שסימן טומאתו בשער צהוב:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:4.english: White hair and spreading - [This refers to a case] where it spread; and [it is] not like a netek [scall], whose sign of impurity is yellow hair.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:5.hebrew: ולמה חלקן הכתוב - בשתי פרשיות, ופירש משפט כל אחת בה, ולא צירפם יחד, שהרי משפטן שוה, והיה לו לכתוב: כי יהיה בו בעורו שחין או מכוה:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:5.english: And why did Scripture divide them - Into two passages, explaining the law of each one separately, rather than combining them together - since their law is the same, and it could have written: "If there is on his skin a boil or a burn."

Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:6.hebrew: שאין מצטרפין זה עם זה - לשיעור נגע כגריס, חצי פול, שאם עלה בו חצי גריס מחמת חום מכה שלא ע"י האור, וחצי גריס אצלה ע"י כויית האור, אין מצטרפין:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:3:6.english: That they do not combine with each other - Regarding the measure of a nega (leprous mark) - the size of a geris, [which is] half a fava bean - [meaning] that if a half-geris arose on it due to the heat of a wound not caused by fire, and a half-geris next to it caused by a burn from fire, they do not combine.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:1.hebrew: שחין - לשון חמימות, כמו (יומא דף נג:) שנה שחונה, וכדמתרגם יונתן חמותי ראיתי אור שחינית (ישעיהו מד):
Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:1.english: Shechin - An expression of heat, as in (Yoma 53b): "a hot year [shanah shechunah]," and as Targum Yonatan translates "chamosi, ra'isi ur" ["I have grown warm, I have seen fire"] as "shechinit" (Isaiah 44).

Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:2.hebrew: לקה באבן - הכהו בכח באבן, אפילו בלא חבורה, דכל מכה מתחמם הבשר מיד ע"י ההכאה:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:2.english: Struck by a stone - [Meaning] he struck him forcefully with a stone, even without a bruise, for with any blow the flesh heats up immediately as a result of the striking.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:3.english: With olive pulp - Because he buried his hand in the waste of olives, which becomes very hot on its own, and he got burned.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:4.hebrew: אבר מעיקרו - ממקום שעוקרים העופרת, והוא חם:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:4.english: A limb from its root - From the place where they detach the lead, and it is hot.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:5.english: Ember - Coal that has not gone out.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:6.english: Ramatz - Hot ash, and that is its name in Arabic as well.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:4:7.english: Gafsit - A type of lime, and they burn it like lime.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:5:1.hebrew: ותניא שחין ומכוה כו' - כולהי הנך מתנייתא מצטרכי הכא לפרושי מאי תיבעי לן, דהא בעיא דלעיל הכי איבעיא לן: ליבן שפוד והכה בו איזה הבל קודם לבא הבל המכה או הבל האור, ונפקא מינה לכדתניא דהולכין אחר האחרון, דתניא שחין ומכוה במקום אחד, באותו מקום שלקה בראשון לקה בשני, באותו גריס עצמו:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:5:1.english: And it is taught: A boil and a burn, etc. - All these baraitot are needed here to explain what was asked of us. For the question above was asked as follows: If one heated a spit and struck [a person] with it, which heat arrived first - the heat of the blow or the heat of the fire? And the practical difference [between the two possibilities] is like what is taught elsewhere, that we follow the latter one - as it is taught: [If] a boil and a burn [occur] in the same place, in that very place where he was struck by the first, he was struck by the second, in that very same bean-sized area.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:5:2.hebrew: ביטל אחרון את הראשון - ונפקא מינה לענין צירוף, שאם היה בו חצי גריס שחין, ולקה באור באותו חצי גריס, נהפך אותו גריס ונעשה מכוה, ואם חזר ולקה לאחר זמן אצל מכוה זו שלא ע"י האור, ונולד בו חצי גריס שחין אחר, ונעשה שלם, אין מצטרף עם הראשון, וטהור, והשתא אהני ליה ביטול, שאילו לא ביטל חצי גריס הראשון, היה זה מצטרף עמו:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:5:2.english: The latter nullifies the former - And there is a practical difference regarding combination: If he had a half-bean-sized area of tzara'at-boil (shechin), and he was struck by fire on that same half-bean area, that bean's area is transformed and becomes a burn (michvah). And if he was later struck again, after some time, near this burn - not by fire - and a different half-bean area of shechin formed there, so that it became a whole [bean-sized area], it does not combine with the first, and he is pure. And now the nullification helped him: for had he not nullified the first half-bean, this [second one] would have combined with it.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:6:1.english: And here, what are the circumstances? - Regarding the dilemma [raised] above, how is it to be asked?

Rashi on Chullin 8a:6:2.hebrew: וליבן שפוד והכה בו - ובהכאה זו יש תורת שחין ותורת מכוה, ואיבעיא לן הי קדים ואתי, דליתי בתרא ונבטליה:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:6:2.english: And he heated a spit and struck him with it - In this single blow there is the legal status of both a boil [she'chin] and a burn [mechavah], and we raised the question of which one arrives first, so that we could nullify whichever came later.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:7:1.hebrew: חבטא קדים - כח ההכאה קדים להרע לו לאדם, והוי שחין, ואתי הבל האור אחרון ומבטל ליה, וה"ל מכוה, ולא מצטרף בהדיה חצי גריס קמא דה"ל שחין ומכוה:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:7:1.english: The blow comes first - The force of the blow acts to harm the person first, and it becomes a shechin (an inflammation from striking); then the heat of the fire comes afterward and nullifies it, so that it becomes a mechavah (a burn) instead; and the first half a grain's-worth [of the wound] does not combine with it - which would [otherwise] have made it a shechin and a mechavah [together, reaching the required size].

Rashi on Chullin 8a:8:1.hebrew: חידוד שאני - דמתוך שהוא חד אין הבל האור שבו חזק, וחתיכתו קדם להבלו:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:8:1.english: Sharpness is different - Since it [the knife] is sharp, the heat of the fire that is in it is not strong, and its cutting precedes its heat.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:9:1.english: Evidently, the blow comes first - and then the heat comes and negates it.

Rashi on Chullin 8a:9:2.hebrew: דברזייה מברז - שלא הכהו בכח, אלא דקרו, ואין כאן חבטא אלא הבל, אבל הכהו דאיכא חבטא, אימא דהא הוה בתרא ומבטל הבלא:
Rashi on Chullin 8a:9:2.english: That he bored him with a boring motion - That he did not strike him with force, but rather pierced him, and there is no impact [chabata] here, only heat. But if he struck him such that there is an impact, one might say that this [the impact] came afterward and nullified the heat.

Tosafot on Chullin 8a:10:1.hebrew: מותר לשחוט בה מקלקל הוא - אע"ג דבסוף פרק אלו דברים בפסחים (דף עג.) מחייב לענין שבת גבי שוחט בשבת בחוץ לעבודת כוכבים משום תיקון כל דהו דתקן, להוציא מידי אבר מן החי, שאני שבת דמלאכת מחשבת אסרה תורה, וכיון שיש תקון פורתא חשיב מלאכת מחשבת שלכך נתכוין, אע"פ שקלקולו יתר על תקונו; אבל לענין נהנה מעבודת כוכבים לא חשיב הנאה, כיון שקלקולו יתר על תקונו:
Tosafot on Chullin 8a:10:1.english: It is permitted to slaughter with it, [since] it is a destructive act - even though at the end of the chapter Eilu Devarim in Pesachim (73a), [the Gemara] holds [one] liable with regard to Shabbat, concerning one who slaughters on Shabbat outside [the Temple courtyard] for idol worship, on account of some minimal repair that he effects, [namely,] to remove it from the status of "a limb from a living animal" - Shabbat is different, for the Torah forbade [only] a purposeful labor (melekhet machsheves), and since there is a small amount of repair, it is considered a purposeful labor, since that is what he intended, even though its damage exceeds its repair; but with regard to benefiting from idol worship, it is not considered a benefit, since its damage exceeds its repair.

Tosafot on Chullin 8a:1:1.hebrew: והא איכא צדדין - משמע מכאן, שאם בשעת שחיטה ניקב הוושט כנגד מה ששחט, טריפה; דהכא הוה בעי למיסר משום צדדין, אי לאו משום דמרווח רווח:
Tosafot on Chullin 8a:1:1.english: But aren't there sides? - This implies from here that if, at the time of slaughter, the esophagus becomes punctured directly opposite the place where he cut, [the animal] is a tereifah; for here [in our Gemara] it would have been necessary to forbid [the animal] on account of the sides, were it not for the fact that [the throat] widens and separates [immediately after the cut].

Tosafot on Chullin 8a:3:1.hebrew: מטמאים בשבוע אחד בשני סימנים בשער לבן ובפסיון - כך דינו: דבסוף שבוע ראשון מטמא אם פשה, או אפי' לא פשה מטמא כי איכא שער לבן, וכן בתחלה מטמא בשער לבן. אבל בסוף שבוע, אם אין שער לבן ולא פשה, אע"ג דעמד בעיניו ולא כהה - טהור, אבל שאר נגעים בעי הסגר פעם שנית. והלשון קצת קשה, דלא הוה ליה למימר "מטמאים" אלא "מטהרים", שאין כן בשאר נגעים דבעו הסגר. וי"ל דה"נ קאמר: מטמא בשער לבן ובפסיון דוקא, אבל אי אין שער לבן ולא פשה, אע"ג דלא כהה - טהור:
Tosafot on Chullin 8a:3:1.english: They become impure within one week via two signs: white hair and spreading - This is its law: that at the end of the first week it becomes impure if it spread, or even if it did not spread it becomes impure when there is white hair, and likewise at the outset it becomes impure via white hair. But at the end of the week, if there is no white hair and it did not spread, even though it remained as it was and did not fade - it is pure; whereas with other nega'im [these conditions] require a second quarantine. And the wording is somewhat difficult, for it should have said not "they become impure" but rather "they become pure", which is not so with other nega'im, which require quarantine. And one may answer that this is indeed what it means: it becomes impure specifically via white hair and spreading; but if there is no white hair and it did not spread, even though it did not fade, it is pure.

Tosafot on Chullin 8a:4:1.hebrew: בחמי טבריא וכל דבר שלא בא מחמת האור - אפילו רבי יוסי דחשיב ליה בפ' כירה (שבת דף לט.) תולדת האור, משום דמיחלפא אפיתחא דגיהנם, שמא כאן היה מודה דנדון משום שחין ולא משום מכוה, כיון דהאי אור בידי שמים:
Tosafot on Chullin 8a:4:1.english: In the hot springs of Tiberias, and anything else that did not come from fire - Even Rabbi Yossi, who considers it, in the chapter "Kirah" (Shabbat 39a), to be a derivative of fire — because [its status] is easily confused with [the fire at] the entrance of Gehinnom — would perhaps concede here that it is judged as [caused by] a sh'chin (boil/skin-eruption) and not as [caused by] a mekhavah (burn), since this fire [i.e., the heat of the hot springs] is [caused] by Heaven [and not by a man-made flame].
